modes.cue_notes: From all fours, walk the hands forward while keeping the hips over the knees. Allow the chest to melt toward the floor, chin or forehead resting on the mat or a bolster. Arms extend forward. The heart center descends as the thoracic spine extends. Keep the hips stacked over the knees — do not let them slide back. A bolster under the chest reduces intensity.

source: Traditional yin yoga; see Paul Grilley, Bernie Clark, Sarah Powers
notes: Targets the thoracic spine extension and anterior shoulder. Heart and lung meridians run the inner arm and chest wall. Counterpose is Child's Pose to neutralize the thoracic extension.
